rationale.oversight-explanation: Decision Bank, code references, and test mappings improved human implementation understanding.
rationale.agent-scope-drift: Decision-linked tests detected departures between programmer intent and agent implementation.
rationale.ai-review: An LLM planner generated decision-specific tests to judge agent-produced implementations.
rationale.rules-based-checks: Executable tests deterministically checked implementation behavior against recorded decisions.
rationale.automation-bias: Baseline programmers passively accepted plans and overlooked decisions despite relevant expertise.
rationale.survey-input: Reports substantive preferences and validation practices for oversight-interface survey items.
rationale.framework: DOP specifies a reusable architecture connecting decisions, agents, code, and tests.
rationale.built-system: Authors implemented Aporia as a working VS Code extension.
rationale.agentic: Agent planned and delivered whole-feature codebase modifications for later validation.
rationale.steering: Questions and Decision Bank substantively shaped generation inputs before implementation.
rationale.risk-overreliance: Study measured passive acceptance, missed decisions, trust, and validation behavior.
rationale.risk-quality: Study measured developers’ mental-model accuracy and implementation comprehensibility.
rationale.method-self-report: Post-task surveys and interviews captured participant experiences and validation strategies.
rationale.method-mining: Telemetry and submitted code quantified decisions and implementation-policy alignment.
rationale.method-experiment: Counterbalanced controlled programming tasks compared Aporia against Claude Code.
